title: Big Ideas in Tech for 2025
edition_framing: Each idea is what a16z partners expect builders to tackle in 2025.
notes: No visible date on the page. Page metadata datePublished 2024-11-15 (may be a draft date); first public appearance not confirmed.

entries.label: The Resurgence of Nuclear
entries.quote: In 2025, I believe we’ll see a surge in demand for nuclear energy.
entries.subject: Nuclear energy demand
entries.author: David Ulevitch

entries.label: The Jobs of the Future: Crossing the Hardware-Software Chasm
entries.quote: In particular, I expect that 2025 will see accelerated demand for: electrical engineers, controls engineers, mechanical and mechatronics engineers, manufacturing engineers, RF engineers, industrial engineers, test engineers, quality engineers, and high-skilled technicians/robotic teleoperators of all types.
entries.subject: Hardware-software engineering jobs
entries.author: Erin Price-Wright

entries.label: “The Catch” Signals the Next Frontier in Space
entries.quote: And we’ll be able to transport humans and cargo around planet Earth in 40 minutes or less, opening up unprecedented industries and access.
entries.subject: Fully reusable heavy-lift launch (Starship)
entries.metric: point-to-point transport time anywhere on Earth
entries.author: Lejla Johnsen
entries.note: No year attached to the 40-minute figure; the entry closes with '2025 could be the beginning of fiction becoming reality.'

entries.label: The Future of Defense Is Decentralized
entries.quote: I expect military decisions will increasingly be made at the edge, where autonomous drones, sensor networks, and battlefield AI systems operate with minimal human intervention.
entries.subject: Autonomous edge decision-making in defense
entries.author: Ryan McEntush

entries.label: XR Devices Get Developer-Ready
entries.quote: I believe XR devices will become a valuable tool in enabling developers to build physical world applications.
entries.subject: Extended reality (XR) devices for developers
entries.author: Oliver Hsu

entries.label: Harnessing Earth Observation Data
entries.quote: The real commercial opportunity lies in developing verticalized products that use Earth observation as just one tool among many to address industry-specific needs.
entries.subject: Vertical Earth observation products
entries.author: Millen Anand
entries.note: Text states the number of Earth observation satellites doubled in five years, from 500 to over 1,000 (current, not a forecast).

entries.label: The Next Phase of Robot Data Collection
entries.quote: Once we’ve collected billions or trillions of tokens of robot data, however, what comes next?
entries.subject: Robot training data and evaluation
entries.author: Jacob Phillips
entries.note: The idea is posed as questions; no direct forecast sentence.

entries.label: New Strides in Free-Space Optical Communications
entries.quote: In 2025, I expect continued advancements in free-space optical communications, driven by nearly inelastic demand for communications bandwidth.
entries.subject: Free-space optical communications
entries.author: Peter Bowman-Davis

entries.label: Big is Back: Tackling Common Diseases (Again)
entries.quote: In 2025, “big is back” in the biopharma world, as even early-stage biotech startups begin to go after big, common diseases again.
entries.subject: Biotech focus on common diseases
entries.author: Vineeta Agarwala

entries.label: Democratizing Health Through Tech
entries.quote: By enabling people to monitor their health proactively, these tech options refocus the healthcare model on prevention, early detection, and keeping healthy patients healthy for longer.
entries.subject: Consumer health technology (biomarkers, wearables, screening)
entries.author: Vijay Pande

entries.label: Super Staffing for Healthcare
entries.quote: We believe 2025 will see specialist AI models serving as “super staffing” platforms in the high stakes environment of healthcare.
entries.subject: AI staffing in healthcare
entries.author: Julie Yoo

entries.label: Drug Targets Are Avocados
entries.quote: Looking to 2025, startups increasingly need an earned secret: a unique insight (head start) around an emerging target; a differentiated approach to hitting a hot one.
entries.subject: Biotech drug target differentiation
entries.author: Jorge Conde

entries.label: The “AI Drummer” and the Promise of Real-Time AI
entries.quote: In the coming year, exciting new use cases will be unlocked: everything from generated video companions to AI bandmates.
entries.subject: Real-time generative AI
entries.author: Anish Acharya

entries.label: AI Video Gets Specialized
entries.quote: In 2025, I expect AI-generated video to become further segmented by use case, giving creators more control and better results.
entries.subject: Specialized AI video generation
entries.author: Bryan Kim

entries.label: The Year of the “AI Brain”
entries.quote: With emerging consumer products tailored to this purpose, in the year ahead I predict more people will begin using AI as an infinite memory bank to guide their decision-making, interactions, and personal growth.
entries.subject: Personal AI memory ("AI brain")
entries.author: Justine Moore

entries.label: Knowledge Work Gets Personalized
entries.quote: I’m excited to see similar controls come to knowledge work.
entries.subject: Personalized AI for knowledge work
entries.author: Olivia Moore

entries.label: Analyzing Qualitative Data with AI
entries.quote: I predict this shift will spawn a new class of analytical tools that seamlessly merge numbers with real-time external context.
entries.subject: AI analysis of qualitative data
entries.author: Zach Cohen

entries.label: An AI Needs a Wallet of One's Own to Act Agentically
entries.quote: As AIs make the transition from NPCs (non-playing characters) to being the main characters, they will begin to act as agents.
entries.subject: Crypto wallets for AI agents
entries.author: Carra Wu

entries.label: Enter “Decentralized Autonomous Chatbots”
entries.quote: But the key point here is decentralization: Running on a permissionless set of nodes, and coordinated by a consensus protocol, the chatbot could even become the first truly autonomous billion-dollar entity.
entries.subject: Decentralized autonomous AI chatbots
entries.author: Dan Boneh and Daniel Reynaud and Daejun Park and Daren Matsuoka
entries.note: Co-authored entry; the four names are listed on the entry.

entries.label: As More People Use AI, We'll Need Unique Proof of Personhood
entries.quote: That’s why the property of privacy-preserving “uniqueness” is the next big idea in building a web we can trust.
entries.subject: Proof of personhood
entries.author: Eddy Lazzarin

entries.label: Going From Prediction Markets to Better Information Aggregation for Everything
entries.quote: Rather, prediction markets set the stage for more distributed technology-based information aggregation mechanisms — which can be used in applications ranging from community governance and sensor networks to finance and much more.
entries.subject: Information aggregation mechanisms (beyond prediction markets)
entries.author: Scott Duke Kominers

entries.label: Enterprises Will Increasingly Accept Stablecoins for Payments
entries.quote: While we’re seeing some enterprise interest in stablecoins (and early adoption in peer-to-peer payments), I expect to see a bigger experimentation wave in 2025.
entries.subject: Enterprise stablecoin payments
entries.author: Sam Broner

entries.label: Countries Explore Putting Government Bonds Onchain
entries.quote: In the U.S. — given that the SEC is set to require clearing treasuries through legacy, burdensome, and costly infrastructure next year — expect more conversations around how blockchains could increase transparency, efficiency, and participation in bonds trading.
entries.subject: Tokenized government bonds
entries.author: Brian Quintenz
entries.note: 'next year' in the quote refers to the SEC treasury clearing requirement, not to the idea itself.

entries.label: We'll See Greater Adoption of the ‘DUNA,’ a New Industry Standard for Blockchain Networks in the U.S.
entries.quote: With the U.S. poised to foster and accelerate progress for its crypto ecosystem in 2025, I expect the DUNA will become a standard for U.S. projects.
entries.subject: DUNA legal structure for blockchain networks
entries.author: Miles Jennings

entries.label: Liquid Democracy Online Goes Physical
entries.quote: We could finally use blockchains to carry out secure, private voting for elections, beginning with low-stakes pilots to limit cybersecurity and auditing concerns.
entries.subject: Blockchain voting and liquid democracy
entries.author: Andrew Hall

entries.label: Builders Will Reuse, Not Just Reinvent, Infrastructure
entries.quote: That’s why I expect more teams to leverage the contributions of others, reusing more off-the-shelf blockchain infrastructure components in 2025 — from consensus protocols and existing staked capital to proof systems.
entries.subject: Reusable blockchain infrastructure components
entries.author: Joachim Neu

entries.label: Crypto Companies Will Begin With the End (-User Experience), Instead of Letting the Infrastructure Determine the UX
entries.quote: In 2025, more crypto product designers will begin with the end-user experience they want, and then choose the appropriate infrastructure from there.
entries.subject: User-experience-first crypto product design
entries.author: Mason Hall

entries.label: “Hiding the Wires” Helps Usher in Web3’s Killer App
entries.quote: That’s why I think our industry will adopt this ethos in 2025: “hide the wires”.
entries.subject: Abstracted crypto UX ("hide the wires")
entries.author: Chris Lyons

entries.label: The Crypto Industry Finally Gets Its Own App Stores, and Discovery
entries.quote: But we may see more of this porting happening in 2025.
entries.subject: Crypto app stores and discovery
entries.author: Maggie Hsu

entries.label: Crypto Owners Become Crypto Users
entries.quote: In 2025, crypto should further develop as a computing movement.
entries.subject: Active crypto usage
entries.author: Daren Matsuoka

entries.label: Various Sectors May Start Tokenizing “Unconventional” Assets
entries.quote: As costs decrease due to maturing infrastructure in the crypto industry and other emerging technologies, the practice of tokenizing assets will spread widely across sectors.
entries.subject: Tokenization of unconventional assets
entries.author: Aaron Schnider

entries.label: When Regulation Becomes Code
entries.quote: Imagine, instead, that those lengthy documents — including text, images, and case precedents — could be used to train regulation-specific LLMs.
entries.subject: Regulation-specific LLMs for compliance
entries.author: Angela Strange

entries.label: Ripping Out Legacy Systems of Record
entries.quote: I predict this sort of cord-cutting — ripping out legacy systems of record in favor of more dynamic upgrades — will be replicated many times over.
entries.subject: Replacement of legacy systems of record
entries.author: Marc Andrusko

entries.label: Differentiation vs. Lasting Defensibility
entries.quote: In 2024, many startups pursued “messy inbox problems” as a wedge to apply LLMs to judgment-intensive tasks. 2025 will be the year of AI companies turning differentiation into lasting defensibility.
entries.subject: AI startup defensibility
entries.author: David Haber

entries.label: AI Advances From Data Collection to Data-in-Action
entries.quote: The next frontier will be AI that not only captures such data for the worker, but then suggests a sequence of actions to take.
entries.subject: AI systems of action for workers
entries.author: Seema Amble

entries.label: Romanticizing Inorganic Growth
entries.quote: While some predict this shift will usher in an era of conventional private equity, where large firms buy and transform assets, I see greater potential in AI-powered, vertical-specific service startups.
entries.subject: AI-powered vertical service roll-ups
entries.author: Joe Schmidt

entries.label: AI-Native UI and UX
entries.quote: I believe 2025 will be the year that AI-native UI and UX paradigms will be established for the next generation of SaaS companies.
entries.subject: AI-native UI and UX
entries.author: Kimberly Tan

entries.label: Every White-Collar Worker Will Have an AI Copilot
entries.quote: I predict 2025 will be the year of AI copilots — eventually, every white-collar role will have one, passing off the most painful parts of their jobs, and freeing up workers to focus on more creative or strategic tasks.
entries.subject: AI copilots for white-collar work
entries.author: James da Costa

entries.label: A Next-Gen Pixar Will Emerge
entries.quote: I believe we’re on the precipice of seeing a next generation Pixar leverage AI-native storytelling formats that blur the lines between film and video games.
entries.subject: AI-native animation and storytelling
entries.author: Jonathan Lai

entries.label: AI Companions With Their Own Inner Worlds
entries.quote: I believe the next generation of companions will become much more engaging and lifelike.
entries.subject: AI companions
entries.author: Andrew Chen

entries.label: Game Tech Powers Tomorrow's Businesses
entries.quote: Whether it’s training autonomous systems in virtual environments, helping consumers shop with 3D visuals, or scaling tomorrow’s workforce via simulations, I think game tech will infuse every sector in 2025.
entries.subject: Game technology in non-game industries
entries.author: Troy Kirwin

entries.label: A Second Wave of “Faceless” Video Creators
entries.quote: For aspiring creators, content that used to require cameras, audio equipment, and green screens can now be replicated with AI software.
entries.subject: Faceless AI-enabled video creators
entries.author: Lester Chen

entries.label: The Decline of "Google It"
entries.quote: The search monopoly ends in 2025.
entries.subject: AI search versus Google search
entries.author: Alex Immerman
entries.note: The text cites Google's ~90% share of US search as the current state.

entries.label: A Golden Era of Sales
entries.quote: New gen AI-powered sales tech will likely automate much of sales reps’ administrative work, making sales organizations significantly more efficient and productive.
entries.subject: AI sales automation
entries.author: Joe Morrissey

entries.label: Beyond GPT Wrappers
entries.quote: I predict 2025 will be the year of the AI-native application layer.
entries.subject: AI-native application layer
entries.author: Sarah Wang

entries.label: Hypercenters: The Regional Race for AI Infrastructure
entries.quote: Over the next five to 10 years, I believe that a world-class Hypercenter will need to develop about three to six gigawatts of installed capacity to keep a seat at the table of frontier AI.
entries.subject: National AI compute infrastructure (AI hypercenters)
entries.horizon: Over the next five to 10 years
entries.metric: installed capacity needed by a world-class AI hypercenter
entries.author: Anjney Midha

entries.label: Small, But Mighty: On-Device AI
entries.quote: In the coming year, I expect smaller, on-device AI models to dominate in terms of volume and usage.
entries.subject: On-device AI models
entries.author: Jennifer Li

entries.label: Beyond "Reason": AI Makes Strides in Math, Physics, and Coding
entries.quote: However, state-of-the-art models are nevertheless showing improved performance on “reasoning” tasks like math, physics, and coding.
entries.subject: LLM reasoning in math, physics and coding
entries.author: Matt Bornstein

entries.label: Generative AI Everywhere
entries.quote: I see AI coming to every application and every device.
entries.subject: On-device generative AI
entries.author: Guido Appenzeller
